07 · The quotations

### Checked, not copied

Every epigraph in the book was checked against a primary source before inclusion: the original text, the original letter or speech, the shareholder letter on the company's own site, or a scholarly edition. Where a beloved quotation could not be verified, it was left out rather than hedged. Proverbs and sayings are labeled as what they are, the property of nobody in particular.

Five famous lines you may expect to find are corrected instead of repeated.

- The line about the survival of "the most adaptable to change," universally attributed to Darwin, appears nowhere in Darwin. It is a 1963 paraphrase by management professor Leon Megginson.

- "It is not enough to be busy; so are the ants" is a misquotation. Thoreau's 1857 sentence to H. G. O. Blake reads "It is not enough to be industrious; so are the ants. What are you industrious about?"

- "It is better to be vaguely right than exactly wrong" belongs to Carveth Read (1898), not Keynes.

- "Price is what you pay; value is what you get" is credited to Ben Graham, because that is how Buffett presents it in his 2008 shareholder letter.

- "Lies, damned lies, and statistics" is given as what it is: a line Mark Twain attributed to Disraeli, with no Disraeli source ever found.

Charlie Munger is quoted twenty times and Warren Buffett fifteen, both at a deliberate cap. Benjamin Franklin, Charles Darwin, Francis Bacon, Seneca, Marcus Aurelius, and Aesop follow. Howard Marks, Ben Graham, and Morgan Housel appear a few times each. Almost everything else is public domain, quoted from public-domain translations, and Sources by Day at the back lists where all 366 come from.

08 · Where it came from

### A daily dose

In 2003, a Swedish businessman named Peter Bevelin published a strange and wonderful book called *Seeking Wisdom: From Darwin to Munger*. He wrote it, he said, to learn: collecting in one place what Darwin, Munger, Buffett, and a hundred scientists and philosophers had figured out about why we misjudge, and how to do better. It became an underground classic among investors and founders, passed hand to hand like a map.

I have read many books on this subject and will read more. This one was born when I asked myself whether there was a book that would provide a daily dose of wisdom, the way a supplement provides a daily dose of vitamins. I could not find one, and in February 2024 I started writing it.

The daily format is old. Tolstoy spent his last years assembling *A Calendar of Wisdom*; a century later, Ryan Holiday's *The Daily Stoic* and Robert Greene's *The Daily Laws* proved the form still works. It works because wisdom is not a download. It is a practice, and practices run on repetition. You cannot read your way into better judgment in a weekend. You might, page by page, over a year, train your way into it.

Three promises. Every quotation was verified against a primary source before it went in. The ideas are credited: where a framing belongs to Munger, Buffett, Housel, Bevelin, or anyone else, their name is on it, and the connective tissue and the mistakes are mine. And nothing here is theory I haven't needed. I have spent my working life building software and companies, and every page is something I learned the expensive way or watched someone else pay for.

I'm Nasser Ghanemzadeh. 17+ years building products and companies across AI, SaaS, and fintech. ### FAQ

#### What is Daily Wisdom?

A year-long course in not fooling yourself. 366 one-page meditations for founders, investors, and managers, in the mental-model tradition of Charlie Munger and Peter Bevelin. Each page holds a verified quotation, a short essay, and one question or action to carry into the day.

#### Who is it for?

Operators who decide for a living: founders watching runway, investors watching themselves, managers building machines that run without them. The three jobs share one craft, making decisions under uncertainty with other people's trust at stake, and the pages rotate among them.

#### How is each day structured?

Three parts on one page. A quotation, checked against its primary source. An essay of about 250 words. A closing prompt, either a question to sit with (Ask yourself) or a small action to take (Try this). Reading the page takes three minutes.

#### What do the twelve months cover?

January builds the latticework of mental models. February and March cover the psychology of misjudgment and its antidotes. April is the mathematics of wisdom. May reads business through Darwin. June is systems and second-order effects. July is the psychology of money, August the investor's temperament, September the manager's craft, October the founder's path. November is the not-to-do list. December asks what all of it is for.

#### Is it out, and in what formats?

Yes. The Kindle edition came out on October 6, 2026, and the paperback and hardcover are on Amazon too. The print editions run 399 pages at 6 by 9 inches. A free sampler, the whole month of November with the not-to-do list and decision journal templates, goes to anyone who joins the newsletter.

#### Is there a list of every day in the book?

Yes. All 366 titles are on this page, month by month, under All 366 pages. Each date has its own link, so you can send someone straight to the page on, say, the Cobra effect (June 8) or the pre-mortem (March 14).

#### How long is it?

366 meditations, one per page, about 104,000 words. The print edition runs 399 pages at 6 by 9 inches. Read one page a day, or raid it before a decision.

#### Are the quotations real?

Yes. Every epigraph was checked against a primary source: the original text, letter, or speech, or the shareholder letter on the company's own site. Where a beloved quotation could not be verified, it was left out. Five famous misattributions are corrected in the book rather than repeated.

#### Do I have to start on January 1?

No. Start on today's date, or anywhere. The year is a circle and you will pass every page eventually. Cross-references point back to the day where an idea was built; ignore them on a first pass.

#### Is this investment advice?

No. The book is for general education. It is not investment, legal, tax, or medical advice, and no reader should act on it without consulting qualified professionals.

### Keep reading

- [All three books](https://ghanemzadeh.com/books/). Daily Wisdom, Forward Deployed AI Engineering, and Founder Mode on one page.

02 · Who this is for

### Three readers

The book is written for three people specifically. The chapters are ordered for each of them in turn.

- **The early-career engineer.** Three to five years into your career. You have read some of the job postings. You recognize something in the description that fits how you want to work. You want a map.

- **The mid-career switcher.** Consultant, solutions architect, product manager, ex-founder. You suspect you already have most of the skills. You want to know what is missing.

- **The founder or hiring manager.** Building an FDE function for the first time. Needs a primer before going to market.

03 · What you'll be able to do

### By the last chapter

The book is the FDE playbook, engineered around four working outcomes. Finish it and a reader should be able to do all four.

- Explain the role to a hiring manager in your own words, without using "forward deployed" as a magic incantation.

- Describe an end-to-end FDE engagement, from the first customer conversation through the production deployment and the synthesis review that turns the engagement into product.

- Execute the first week of a real engagement using the templates in the workbook at the back of the book.

- Plan a credible path from your current role to a first offer, with a portfolio you can defend and an interview loop you can prepare for.

04 · Structure

### Five parts

**Part I. The Landscape.** What the role is, where it came from, and why the AI moment has made it the default operating model of the industry.

**Part II. The Mindset and the Method.** The four traits that distinguish people who succeed at this work. The Echo and Delta split that organizes the work into two halves of one craft. The three-phase engagement that gives the work its rhythm. The gravel-road-to-highway pattern that makes the work compound into product.

**Part III. The Craft.** Discovery, evaluation, shipping the first slice, integrating with the enterprise stack, and closing the loop.

**Part IV. Becoming an FDE.** The paths in. The portfolio. The interview loop. The first year on the inside.

**Part V. Economy and Future.** Pricing, outcomes, contracts. Cargo cults and failure modes. The FDE diaspora the labs are producing whether they want to or not. A closing note for the buyer.

05 · Anchor chapters

### Selected chapters

#### The Pilot-to-Production Gap

Why 95% of enterprise AI pilots produce zero measurable return, and why the gap isn't closed by buying more tokens.

#### A Brief History: From Palantir to the Frontier Labs

Two decades of FDE practice at Palantir. How it escaped that niche and became the default model for OpenAI, Anthropic, and the labs that followed.

#### Echo and Delta: Two Halves of One Craft

Echo is the deployment that's working now. Delta is the change that makes the next one work better. Most engineers are good at one. FDEs do both.

#### Scope, Validate, Deliver: The Three-Phase Engagement

The rhythm every FDE engagement follows, and the specific moves at each phase that separate the engagements that ship from the ones that drift.

#### Evals as Specification

In FDE work the eval is the spec. How to write one that customers will sign, engineers can build against, and the model can be measured on.

#### The FDE Interview Loop

What the loop actually tests. The case study, the writing sample, the customer simulation. How to prepare for each, with worked examples.

#### Pricing, Outcomes, and Contracts

Day rates, project rates, outcome rates, and equity. When each works. The contractual language that protects both sides.

#### Cargo Cults and Failure Modes

The five ways FDE engagements fail. Each one is recoverable if you catch it by the second week.

06 · Why now

### A snapshot in motion

Most of the canonical literature on the role was written between September 2025 and April 2026. Some of it was written while this book was being drafted. The Anthropic and Blackstone joint venture, the OpenAI Deployment Company, the Google Cloud hires, the Big Four repositionings were news, not history, when the manuscript was working through draft. The book is written to still be useful three years from now, but the snapshot dimension is real, and a reader picking it up in 2029 will need to interpret the contemporary references through whatever has happened by then.

One principle is most likely to outlast the specific organizations and titles around it. **The artifact is the truth. The code shipping is the substance. The document is the imitation.** Everything else in the book is an unpacking of that.

### FAQ

#### Who is this book for?

Three readers in particular. Early-career engineers (3 to 5 years in) who recognize something in the FDE job description that fits how they want to work. Mid-career switchers (consultants, solutions architects, PMs, ex-founders) who suspect they already have most of the skills. Founders and hiring managers building an FDE function for the first time. If none of those descriptions fits you, the book has failed at scoping.

#### How long is it and how is it organized?

304 pages, organized into five parts and 20 chapters: the landscape, the mindset and method, the craft, becoming an FDE, and the economy and future. Plus a workbook and annotated references at the back.

#### Why this book instead of the other AI books?

Most AI books are about the models. This one is about the practice of deploying them inside someone else's company, with all the customer-side friction that implies. It is also written from inside that work, not from the bench.

#### When is it available?

First edition, May 2026. The current version is 1.5, August 2026. The full Kindle and paperback editions are available now on Amazon, and you can subscribe to the launch list above to read the first chapters.

#### What formats?

Kindle and paperback are both available now on Amazon. You can also read the first chapters by subscribing to the launch list.

#### Is this affiliated with Palantir, OpenAI, or Anthropic?

No. Independent publication. The book discusses these organizations because they shape the role, but the author is not affiliated with any of them. Views are the author's alone.

# AI Discovery Day: 2-Hour Use-Case Scoping Session ($500)

URL: https://ghanemzadeh.com/discovery-day/

Optional. Most founders start with the [free 15-minute Scoping Call](https://ghanemzadeh.com/call/).

Discovery Day

## Before we scope a Sprint, we scope the problem.

A 2-hour working session with Nasser Ghanemzadeh. We look at your use case, your data, your codebase, and your team. By the end you have either a clean Sprint Brief or an honest "this isn't a Sprint yet, here's what to do first" memo.

$500. Credited toward your Sprint if you continue within 14 days.

[Book a Discovery Day →](https://cal.com/ghanemzadeh/discovery)

Next available slot: visible on the booking page. One Discovery Day per week max.

As covered in

Forbes · TechCrunch · Al Jazeera · HuffPost

02 · The document

### What you walk away with

By the end of the 2 hours you have a working document with all of the following, written on the call and ready to forward to your team.

- Use-case clarification, written in a single sentence using the Sprint Brief template.

- Data and API readiness assessment for the candidate workflow.

- Recommended workflow scope (or a recommended deferment, with reasoning).

- A value estimate: what the workflow is worth a year in your numbers, and how long the Sprint takes to pay back.

- A go / no-go memo on whether a Sprint is the right next step.

- A Sprint Brief draft if there's a strong fit, including success criteria and out-of-scope items.

- Honest answers about what fits in 10 business days and what doesn't.

03 · Fit

### Who this is for

- B2B SaaS founders or product leaders considering shipping an AI feature.

- Teams that have tried building AI features and gotten stuck somewhere between prototype and production.

- Teams that know AI should be part of their product but want a second opinion before committing engineering time.

- Teams comparing Sprint vendors and wanting to validate fit before signing.

### Who this is not for

- Teams looking for a generic AI strategy consultation.

- Solo indie hackers without a B2B SaaS product.

- Enterprise teams with formal procurement or RFP processes.

- Anyone who wants a quick first conversation. Start with the [free 15-minute Scoping Call](https://ghanemzadeh.com/call/).

04 · The two hours

### How a Discovery Day works

The 2 hours are structured but not rigid. Rough shape:

**Minutes 0–30: Your context.** Current product, team, AI experiments to date, what's worked and what hasn't, what's pulling the AI conversation forward inside your company.

**Minutes 30–75: The candidate workflow.** Inputs, outputs, users, data sources, current manual process, what good output looks like, who reviews it before it ships.

**Minutes 75–105: Feasibility.** What fits in a 10-day Sprint and what doesn't. Risk classification (low / medium / high). Integration complexity. Where the Day-5 prototype likely lands.

**Minutes 105–120: The memo.** Go / no-go recommendation, Sprint Brief draft (if applicable), scoping language, next-step recommendation. Shared as a Google Doc you keep.

About half of Discovery Days end with a Sprint recommendation. The other half end with "here's what to do first, come back when X is in place." Both are valid outcomes. The point of a Discovery Day is to find out which one you are, not to convince you to buy a Sprint.

05 · The credit

### The credit toward Sprint

If you continue to a full Sprint within 14 days of your Discovery Day, the $500 is credited against the Sprint price.

So a Discovery Day followed by a Sprint costs the Sprint price, not the Sprint price plus $500.

If we agree the Sprint isn't the right next step, the $500 covers the working document and the 2 hours. No upsell, no follow-up sequence, no retainer pitch.

06 · Before the call

### What I need from you before the call

A short pre-call form, sent after booking. Three things:

- **The workflow you're considering.** One paragraph is enough. Examples I've worked through with other founders: investor update assistant, runway scenario explainer, customer summary generator, support ticket triage, onboarding assistant.

- **Your stack and data access.** What's your product built in, where does the relevant data live (Stripe, your DB, HubSpot, Linear, Notion, your CRM, your admin), and what AI provider you already use (Anthropic, OpenAI, Bedrock, Vertex) if any.

- **The decision-maker question.** Who needs to approve a Sprint, and are they on the call. If they're not, a Discovery Day is fine, but the Sprint recommendation will be harder to act on.

That's it. No data dumps, no NDAs to sign before the call. We sign a mutual NDA on the call itself if either side wants one.

07 · Who's behind it

### Why work with me

I'm Nasser Ghanemzadeh. I've spent 17+ years on the customer side of software, as CEO, CPO, and product lead. I built and exited Nivo (200K+ users, 450% revenue growth, acquired), led product at Pangouan, co-founded Iran Startups, and founded Finnova, where I was the first managing director. These days I build Vectig, an AI-native startup finance product, shipped daily with Claude Code and MCP.

**Speaking on AI-native product development:** OMR Festival, re:publica, GITEX EUROPE.

A Discovery Day points that experience at your roadmap for two hours. Based in Turkey, available across European, Middle Eastern, and North American business hours.

[LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ghanemzadeh/) · [Email](mailto:ghanemzadeh@gmail.com) · [Vectig](https://vectig.com)

### FAQ

#### What if we decide not to do a Sprint after the Discovery Day?

Then you walk away with the working document, the go / no-go memo, and 2 hours of focused outside-perspective on your AI roadmap. No follow-up sales sequence. You're free to take the memo to another vendor, to your internal team, or to nobody at all.

#### Do you sign an NDA?

If either side wants a mutual NDA, we sign one on the call itself before getting into specifics. I don't ask for NDAs to be signed before booking, and I don't expect you to.

#### What if our data isn't ready?

That's one of the most common Discovery Day outcomes: "the workflow makes sense, but the data foundation isn't there yet." The memo will say exactly what to do first, usually a 2 to 4 week data-readiness project that you can run internally, and we revisit Sprint readiness when it's done.

#### How is this different from the free Scoping Call?

The Scoping Call is free and takes 15 minutes: we pick the workflow and check whether your data can carry it in ten days. The Discovery Day is a paid two-hour working session that ends with a written document you keep: the scope, a go/no-go memo, and a Sprint Brief draft if there is a fit. Most founders start with the call.

#### What if I'm not sure I want a Sprint yet?

Then a Discovery Day is exactly the right starting point. About half of them end with a deferment recommendation. That's a feature, not a failure mode.

#### Can a co-founder or technical lead join?

Yes. Up to three people from your side on the call. Beyond three the conversation slows down. If you want broader team alignment, the right pattern is: founder + tech lead on the Discovery Day, then I record a Loom walkthrough of the memo for everyone else.

#### What if our use case is in a high-risk category (legal, medical, compliance, payments)?

The Discovery Day still works, but the Sprint recommendation will likely be "not yet" or "redefine scope to a lower-risk adjacent workflow." High-risk first Sprints don't make sense for teams new to AI deployment. The memo will explain what does.

#### Do you work with companies outside B2B SaaS?

Mostly no. The methodology, examples, and Sprint structure are built around founder-led B2B SaaS at 5 to 50 people, post-product-market-fit. If you're outside that, the Discovery Day may still be useful but the Sprint may not be the right vehicle.

Book a Discovery Day for a focused outside read on whether the AI feature you're considering is ready to ship in 10 business days. Or start with the full breakdown of the [10-day FDE Sprint](https://ghanemzadeh.com/ai-feature-sprint/).

# FDE as a Service: 33 Providers and What They Charge (2026)

URL: https://ghanemzadeh.com/fde-as-a-service/

[Forward Deployed Engineer](https://ghanemzadeh.com/forward-deployed-ai-engineer/)

## FDE as a service: who sells forward deployed engineers, and what it costs

FDE as a service means buying a forward deployed engineer's time or output from an outside provider instead of hiring one. I checked the own pages of 33 providers on October 14, 2026: model and platform vendors, consultancies, talent marketplaces, and independents. Only 8 publish a price. Where they do, an embedded engineer costs about $15,000 to $40,000 a month, a senior builder through a marketplace about $25,000 a month, and hourly contractors from $29 to $99 an hour depending on where the engineer lives.

By [Nasser Ghanemzadeh](https://ghanemzadeh.com/). Checked October 14, 2026. [Download the data (CSV)](https://ghanemzadeh.com/assets/data/fde-as-a-service-providers-2026-10-14.csv). Disclosure: I sell one of these, the [FDE Sprint](https://ghanemzadeh.com/ai-feature-sprint/). It is described separately below and not counted or ranked in the list.

### Two different jobs share the name

Read the offers closely and "FDE as a service" means one of two things:

- **An engineer who builds AI for you.** The FDE embeds in your team and ships AI into your product or operations. The vendor arms, most consultancies, and the independents sell this.

- **An engineer who staffs your customer deployments.** Software companies that need FDEs at their own customers rent them under their brand. A.Team Deployed, Appsierra, Brilliantech, and several marketplaces sell this.

Check which one a provider means before comparing prices.

### What the market looks like

- **Most sell time, not outcomes.** The common unit is an embedded engineer by the month or the hour. Fixed-scope offers are rare: Orq.ai's four-week, one-agent engagement on its own platform, Dinacode's fixed cost per sprint, and pilots from CHI Software, Brilliantech, and Phos AI Labs.

- **Prices are mostly hidden.** 25 of 33 providers publish no price, including every large vendor. Several sell through AWS Marketplace private offers.

- **Guarantees are about people, not results.** Replacement guarantees are common (Uvik Software, AY Automate, Uplers), and Terminal and Index.dev offer risk-free trial periods. Only Adaptive ML mentions a money-back guarantee tied to delivery.

- **Vendor arms come with a platform.** OpenAI, AWS, Microsoft, Anthropic's services company, Vercel, Adaptive ML, and Orq.ai build on their own models or platforms.

### Every published price

The 8 providers that show a price on their own page, quoted as published.

| Provider | Type | Price as published | How you pay |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Brilliantech | Consultancy | POCs from $8,000; embedded $15,000 to $40,000 a month; multi-site pods from $50,000 | Pilot, monthly embed, or pod |
| Phos AI Labs | Consultancy | Audit from $10,000; embedded delivery from $15,000 a month (its homepage says from $10,000 a month) | Audit, then monthly embed |
| AY Automate | Consultancy | Single embedded FDE from $60,000 a year | Full-time embedded engineer |
| Uvik Software | Consultancy | $50 to $99 an hour by role; engagements start at $25,000 (the page shows slightly different bands in places) | Hourly, monthly statement of work |
| Beetroot | Consultancy | $65 to $95 an hour on sample FDE profile cards | Time-boxed mission |
| A.Team | Marketplace | About $25,000 a month for a senior builder, fully loaded | Monthly, per engagement |
| Second Talent | Marketplace | From $29 an hour, payroll and equipment included | Hourly |
| Uplers | Marketplace | "Starts at $2500" (the page doesn't say per what) | Contract or full-time |

### Model and platform vendors (7)

AI labs and platform companies selling their own engineers to their customers. None publishes a price, and the work runs on their own models or platform. OpenAI and Microsoft aim at enterprises; Anthropic's services company at mid-sized companies.

- **[OpenAI Deployment Company](https://openai.com/index/openai-launches-the-deployment-company/)**A majority-owned OpenAI business that places forward deployed engineers inside customer organizations. It is acquiring Tomoro for about 150 FDEs, subject to regulatory approval. How you pay: Engagement, enterprise · Price: Not published · Terms: Starts with a diagnostic, then a few priority workflows

- **[AWS Forward Deployed Engineering](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/aws/aws-1-billion-forward-deployed-ai-engineers)**A $1 billion AWS unit that embeds AWS engineers with customers to build agentic AI systems in the customer's AWS account. How you pay: Engagement · Price: Not published · Terms: "Structured around shared goals and business results, not billable hours"

- **[Microsoft Frontier Company](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/frontier-company)**A Microsoft business built on the FDE model that embeds Microsoft engineering, industry, and AI staff inside customer organizations. How you pay: Engagement, enterprise · Price: Not published · Terms: Tied to business outcomes

- **[Anthropic's enterprise AI services company](https://www.anthropic.com/news/enterprise-ai-services-company)**A services firm backed by Anthropic with Blackstone, Hellman & Friedman, and Goldman Sachs, in which Anthropic's Applied AI engineers and the firm's own engineers build Claude systems. Anthropic's page does not use the term forward deployed. How you pay: Engagement, mid-sized companies · Price: Not published · Terms: Not stated

- **[Vercel](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prodview-d2r2q5noszttm)**Vercel's own forward deployed engineers, embedded for Vercel and Next.js migrations, performance work, and AI builds on its platform. How you pay: Private offer on AWS Marketplace · Price: Not published · Terms: Not stated

- **[Adaptive ML](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prodview-tt2xc7rn4pkfe)**Forward deployed ML engineers who fine-tune and deploy models and agents on Adaptive ML's platform inside the customer's cloud. How you pay: Private offer on AWS Marketplace · Price: Not published · Terms: "Outcome-backed delivery with a money-back guarantee"

- **[Orq.ai](https://orq.ai/solutions/forward-deployed-engineering)**Orq.ai's engineers work inside the customer's team for four weeks to ship one AI agent on the customer's stack, using Orq.ai's LLM platform. How you pay: Fixed four-week engagement · Price: Not published · Terms: One AI agent shipped to production in four weeks

### Consultancies and services firms (18)

The largest group. Most sell an embedded senior engineer or a small pod by the month or under a statement of work, and most quote prices after a call.

- **[Brilliantech](https://brilliantechsoft.com/staff-augmentation-services/hire-forward-deployed-engineer)**An India-based staff augmentation firm that embeds FDEs, including in a software company's customer environments. How you pay: Pilot, monthly embed, or pod · Price: POCs from $8,000; embedded $15,000 to $40,000 a month; multi-site pods from $50,000 · Terms: Proposal within 24 hours of a free consultation

- **[Phos AI Labs](https://phosailabs.com/blog/best-forward-deployed-ai-engineers)**A US AI consulting firm describing its work as FDE-caliber embedded delivery. The prices come from a ranking post in which it lists itself first. How you pay: Audit, then monthly embed · Price: Audit from $10,000; embedded delivery from $15,000 a month (its homepage says from $10,000 a month) · Terms: Aimed at US mid-market companies with $5M+ revenue

- **[AY Automate](https://www.ayautomate.com/services/forward-deployed-engineers)**An AI automation firm that places a full-time, nearshore embedded FDE and quotes narrower engagements after a call. How you pay: Full-time embedded engineer · Price: Single embedded FDE from $60,000 a year · Terms: Placement in 2 to 4 weeks; 90-day replacement guarantee

- **[Uvik Software](https://uvik.net/technologies/hire-forward-deployed-engineers/)**A Tallinn-headquartered software company that places its in-house senior engineers as embedded FDEs. How you pay: Hourly, monthly statement of work · Price: $50 to $99 an hour by role; engagements start at $25,000 (the page shows slightly different bands in places) · Terms: 30 days notice, no auto-renew; 30-day free replacement; profiles within 48 hours

- **[Beetroot](https://beetroot.co/services/forward-deployed-engineering/)**A software services company with engineers in Ukraine, Poland, Bulgaria, and Vietnam, building LLM workflows, RAG, and agentic systems. How you pay: Time-boxed mission · Price: $65 to $95 an hour on sample FDE profile cards · Terms: 1 to 2 week assessment, 1 to 3 month embed, then handoff

- **[Entrans](https://www.entrans.ai/solutions/fde-as-a-service)**Sells "FDE as a Service" for AI agent deployment, legacy modernization, and systems integration. Its cost guide puts the market at $15,000 to $40,000 a month. How you pay: PoC sprint or long-term embed · Price: Not published · Terms: Aimed at enterprises

- **[CHI Software](https://chisw.com/ai/forward-deployed-engineering-services/)**A software development company selling phased FDE engagements with senior engineers on-site or remote, aimed at regulated enterprises. How you pay: Fixed-scope pilot, then phased · Price: Not published · Terms: Pilot with fixed scope and a written risk assessment

- **[ClearScale](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prodview-3zfqx7y7cew2w)**An AWS Premier partner selling one dedicated lead FDE as a fixed monthly commitment. How you pay: Monthly subscription on AWS Marketplace · Price: Flat monthly fee for one lead FDE; amount not public · Terms: Private offers for multi-FDE pods

- **[Jefferson Frank](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prodview-ccwm56w43gwpy)**Sells one dedicated AWS-certified FDE embedded in the buyer's team, backed by AWS architects. How you pay: Monthly subscription on AWS Marketplace · Price: "Predictable monthly pricing"; amount not public · Terms: Not stated

- **[The Cloud Catalysts](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prodview-5l5gdtn27ipa4)**Embeds an FDE from its delivery network for AI and AWS builds. How you pay: Statement of work on AWS Marketplace · Price: Not published · Terms: Free discovery assessment

- **[Sia Partners](https://www.sia-partners.com/en/our-capabilities/forward-deployed-engineering-a-service)**A management consultancy selling FDE as a service in three formats for enterprises. How you pay: Single FDE, squad, or platform rollout · Price: Not published · Terms: Scoped within two weeks to a build path with a first milestone

- **[IBM Consulting](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-05-14-A-New-Way-to-Make-AI-Actually-Work-in-the-Real-World)**Small senior pods of specialists working with AI agents, embedded with client teams on IBM's delivery platform. How you pay: Forward Deployed Units · Price: Not published · Terms: Not stated

- **[HatchWorks AI](https://hatchworks.com/forward-deployed-engineers/)**An AI services firm embedding a senior AI FDE or a small delivery team, plus a fractional Chief AI Officer offer. How you pay: Single FDE or team · Price: Not published · Terms: Not stated

- **[&above](https://www.andabove.com/services/forward-deployed-engineers)**A London AI build partner that hires and manages senior AI engineers and embeds them in UK client teams. How you pay: Embedded engineers against a scoped workflow · Price: Not published · Terms: "In weeks"

- **[Nextbrick](https://nextbrick.com/services/forward-deployed-engineers)**An enterprise search and AI company selling its senior engineers as embedded FDEs. How you pay: Outcome-scoped engagement · Price: Not published · Terms: Scoped around results, not hours

- **[Dinacode](https://www.dinacode.com/en/forward-deployed-engineer)**A Valencia software studio whose embedded engineers audit a workflow, then build AI agents for it. How you pay: Fixed cost per sprint · Price: Fixed per sprint; amount not published · Terms: Two-week audit, first agent in production in 4 to 8 weeks

- **[Appsierra](https://www.appsierra.com/hire/hire-forward-deployed-engineers)**An India-based firm selling an embedded engineer or pod to work inside a software company's customer accounts. How you pay: Engineer or pod · Price: Quoted after a call · Terms: Paid pilot; "cancel anytime"

The $8,000 to $30,000 a month on its page is described as the market rate, not its own price. How you pay: Monthly retainer or fixed 6-week cycle · Price: Not published · Terms: "Built in 6 weeks"

### Talent marketplaces (7)

Platforms that match you with a contract, fractional, or full-time FDE. Several are built for software companies that need FDEs at their own customers, not for teams that want AI built for themselves.

- **[A.Team](https://www.a.team/hire-forward-deployed-engineers)**A talent network supplying senior engineers or pods that embed at a software company's own customers, under that company's brand. How you pay: Monthly, per engagement · Price: About $25,000 a month for a senior builder, fully loaded · Terms: Named, priced profiles in 3 to 5 business days

- **[Second Talent](https://www.secondtalent.com/hire-developers/forward-deployed-engineer/)**An Asia-focused hiring and employer-of-record platform placing remote FDEs from Vietnam, the Philippines, India, and elsewhere with US startups. How you pay: Hourly · Price: From $29 an hour, payroll and equipment included · Terms: Shortlist in 24 hours

- **[Uplers](https://www.uplers.com/hire-forward-deployed-engineers/)**An India-focused hiring platform that shortlists FDEs and handles payroll and legal work for India hires. How you pay: Contract or full-time · Price: "Starts at $2500" (the page doesn't say per what) · Terms: 30 days cancellation; replacement guarantees; 3 to 5 candidates in 48 hours

- **[Index.dev](https://www.index.dev/hire/forward-deployed-engineer)**Matches vetted FDEs from Latin America and Central and Eastern Europe, pitched at SaaS companies scaling AI adoption. How you pay: Month-to-month contract, direct hire, or pod · Price: Not published · Terms: 30-day risk-free trial; "in 48 hours"

- **[Terminal](https://www.terminal.io/hire-developers/forward-deployed-engineers)**A nearshore hiring platform offering vetted FDEs from Latin America and Canada. How you pay: Contract, contract-to-hire, or full-time · Price: Not published · Terms: 14-day risk-free guarantee on contracts

- **[Go Fractional](https://www.gofractional.com/hire/forward-deployed-engineer)**A fractional-talent network matching companies with part-time FDEs, with contract-to-hire and interim options. How you pay: Monthly retainer · Price: Not published · Terms: Matches in as little as 3 days; no recruiting fees

- **[South](https://www.hireinsouth.com/roles/forward-deployed-engineer)**A Latin America hiring service that sources and pays remote FDEs for US companies. How you pay: Full-time placement · Price: Not published · Terms: Pay only if you hire; shortlist in 7 to 10 days

### Independents (1)

One-person practices selling their own time. Few show up in search yet; the ones that do sell retainers or fixed-scope pilots.

- **[Rohit Raj](https://rohitraj.tech/services/fractional-forward-deployed-engineer)**A solo AI engineer in Bengaluru selling a fractional FDE retainer, with a fixed-scope pilot as a way in. How you pay: Fractional retainer or fixed-scope pilot · Price: Not published · Terms: Two fixed days a week, minimum 3 months

### Rate cards from the market

Four published estimates of what FDE time costs in general. Each publisher sells FDE services or training, so read them as their view of the market, not a neutral survey.

- [Second Talent, cost to hire](https://www.secondtalent.com/cost-to-hire/forward-deployed-engineer/): US freelance or contract FDE: $95 to $142 an hour junior, $119 to $185 mid-level, $155 to $235 senior.

- [Entrans, FDE cost guide](https://www.entrans.ai/blog/forward-deployed-engineer-cost): FDE as a service $15,000 to $40,000 a month; offshore $5,000 to $15,000 a month; contractors $60 to $250 an hour.

- [ILMTEC, FDE-as-a-service cost guide](https://ilmtec.ai/blog/forward-deployed-engineering-as-a-service-cost/): $8,000 to $30,000 per engineer per month.

- [fde.academy, fractional FDE guide](https://fde.academy/blog/fractional-forward-deployed-engineer-for-startups): Fractional FDEs at $250 to $400+ an hour (guidance for engineers setting rates, not a survey).

For a full-time hire, job postings in October 2026 put the median US posted base range at $180,000 to $250,208 ([260 roles analyzed](https://ghanemzadeh.com/forward-deployed-engineer-job-market/)). The [FDE cost calculator](https://ghanemzadeh.com/fde-cost-calculator/) turns that into a first-year cost per shipped workflow.

### How to choose

- **You're an enterprise committed to one AI platform:** that vendor's deployment arm.

- **You need an engineer embedded for months and have $15,000+ a month:** a consultancy or a marketplace contractor.

- **You need ongoing help a few days a week:** a fractional FDE on a retainer.

- **You need FDEs at your own customers:** a marketplace built for that, such as A.Team Deployed.

- **You haven't shipped your first AI workflow yet:** a fixed-scope engagement first, so you learn what the role would do before paying for it every month.

### Where my offer fits

The [FDE Sprint](https://ghanemzadeh.com/ai-feature-sprint/) is the fixed-scope model, sized for founder-led B2B SaaS teams of 5 to 50: one AI workflow shipped into your product in ten business days, at a fixed $5,000, with a full refund if there's no working prototype on your data by Day 5 or the workflow isn't running to its acceptance criteria by Day 10. It is independent of any model vendor. It is not a monthly embed, and it doesn't staff your customer deployments.

### How this list was made

On October 14, 2026, I searched for providers selling forward deployed engineers to other companies and read each provider's own page. A provider is listed only if that page offers FDE work to buyers; prices are quoted only as they appear there. Excluded: Palantir (FDEs come bundled with its platform deals), Google Cloud and Anthropic's direct FDE team (careers pages only), Toptal and Upwork (no FDE hire page found), and firms whose only mention of FDE work is a blog post. Where a page contradicts itself, the listing says so. Providers change pages often; corrections are welcome by [email](mailto:ghanemzadeh@gmail.com).

[Download the data (CSV, 33 providers)](https://ghanemzadeh.com/assets/data/fde-as-a-service-providers-2026-10-14.csv). Free to reuse with credit under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).

### Frequently asked questions

#### What is FDE as a service?

FDE as a service means buying a forward deployed engineer's time or output from an outside provider instead of hiring one. The engineer embeds in your team, works in your codebase and data, and ships working software. In October 2026 it is sold by model and platform vendors' deployment arms, consultancies, talent marketplaces, and independent engineers.

#### How much does FDE as a service cost?

Of the 33 providers checked on October 14, 2026, 8 publish a price. Embedded engineers from consultancies run about $15,000 to $40,000 a month (Brilliantech, Phos AI Labs), a senior builder through A.Team is about $25,000 a month, and hourly rates run from $29 for Asia-based engineers (Second Talent) to $50 to $99 (Uvik Software). Pilots start around $8,000 to $10,000. The large vendors publish no prices.

#### What is the difference between FDE as a service and a fractional FDE?

FDE as a service usually means a full-time embedded engineer billed by the month. A fractional FDE works part-time on a retainer, for example two fixed days a week for at least three months, with scope that moves as the work goes.

#### Should a startup buy FDE as a service or hire a forward deployed engineer?

Hire when you'll need the role for years and can wait months to fill it. Buy outside FDE time when the need is a project, or you need it now. If the first AI workflow hasn't shipped yet, start with a fixed-scope engagement so you learn what the role would do before paying for it every month. The FDE cost calculator compares a hire, a contractor, and a fixed-price Sprint.

#### Which FDE providers work with startups?

Mostly the marketplaces. A.Team, Index.dev, Uplers, and Second Talent all pitch startups or SaaS companies, though A.Team Deployed is built for software companies staffing their own customer deployments. The vendor arms and most consultancies aim at enterprises or the mid-market.

# FDE Cost Calculator: Hire vs Contractor vs Sprint

URL: https://ghanemzadeh.com/fde-cost-calculator/

[Forward Deployed Engineer for startups](https://ghanemzadeh.com/forward-deployed-engineer-for-startups/)

## What does a forward deployed engineer cost?

In year one, less than the salary suggests and more than a contract looks. Put in how many AI workflows you need shipped this year, and the calculator compares a full-time hire, a contractor, and a fixed-price FDE Sprint on three numbers: first-year cost, cost per workflow, and time to the first workflow in production.

By [Nasser Ghanemzadeh](https://ghanemzadeh.com/). Last updated October 2026.

### Your numbers

Every field is editable. It runs in your browser; nothing you type leaves this page.

### The comparison

| Option | First-year cost | Cost per workflow | Time to the first workflow |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hire full-time | $158,333 | $79,167 | 4 months to hire, then the build |
| Contractor | $48,000 | $24,000 | About 4 weeks of build, once you have found one |
| FDE Sprint | Two Sprints at $5,000 each | $5,000 | Ten business days |

The figures above are the worked example below, with the default inputs. Change any input to recalculate.

### How the numbers are calculated

- **Hire full-time.** Salary times the overhead multiple, for the months of the first year left after hiring and onboarding. Cost per workflow divides that by the workflows you need. The first workflow ships after the hiring months plus its own build.

- **Contractor.** Hourly rate times hours per workflow, times the number of workflows. Time to the first workflow assumes 40 billable hours a week, after you have found and contracted someone.

- **FDE Sprint.** The fixed Sprint price, once per workflow. Each Sprint ships one workflow into your repo in ten business days, with a full refund if there is no working prototype by Day 5 or the workflow isn't running to its acceptance criteria by Day 10.

**Worked example, with the defaults.** Two workflows. A hire at $190,000 base and a 1.25 overhead multiple, who joins after four months, costs $190,000 × 1.25 × 8/12 = $158,333 in the first year, or $79,167 per workflow. A contractor at $150 an hour for 160 hours a workflow costs $24,000 per workflow, $48,000 for both. Two Sprints cost twice the Sprint price, $5,000 each.

Median US total compensation for the role is about $206,000 ([Levels.fyi](https://www.levels.fyi/t/software-engineer/title/forward-deployed-engineer)), so if you plan to match the market on total pay rather than base, raise the salary field. Posted ranges run higher still: in [260 live roles in October 2026](https://ghanemzadeh.com/forward-deployed-engineer-job-market/), the median US posted base range was $180,000 to $250,208.

### What the calculator leaves out

Cost per workflow is the fair way to compare the first few workflows, and an unfair way to compare everything after that. A full-time engineer also maintains what shipped, iterates on it when the model or your data changes, and starts the next workflow without a new contract. A contractor's cost goes up if the scope drifts, and down if the scope is already tight. A Sprint ships one narrow workflow and hands it to your team with a rubric, a playbook, and a recorded walkthrough, so it only works if someone on your team will own the result.

So read the break-even line, not just the cheapest column. If you need more workflows a year than the break-even, and AI is a standing part of the roadmap, hire. If you need one or two, or you want to learn what an AI workflow takes before you write a job description, start with a Sprint. [The three options, compared in full](https://ghanemzadeh.com/forward-deployed-engineer-for-startups/).

The calculator also leaves out buying an embedded FDE by the month. Where consultancies publish a price, it runs about $15,000 to $40,000 a month; the [FDE-as-a-service market map](https://ghanemzadeh.com/fde-as-a-service/) lists 33 providers and their terms.

### Frequently asked questions

#### How much does a forward deployed engineer cost?

Job postings in 2026 put a forward deployed engineer's base salary typically between $160,000 and $220,000, with a median near $190,000, and median US total compensation is about $206,000. The cost to the company in the first year is different: benefits and payroll taxes add to it, and the months spent hiring take away from it, because nobody is paid or shipping yet. That first-year cost is what this calculator adds up.

#### Is a Sprint cheaper than hiring a forward deployed engineer?

Per workflow, yes, for the first several. But a hire is a different purchase: standing capacity to maintain, iterate, and ship the next workflow without a new contract. The calculator shows the break-even point, the number of workflows a year at which a hire costs less per workflow than Sprints. Below it, start with a Sprint. Well above it, hire.

#### Where do the calculator's defaults come from?

The salary default is the 2026 median base from Recruiting from Scratch's analysis of forward deployed engineer job postings. The other defaults are example inputs, not market data: replace the overhead, hiring time, contractor rate, and hours with your own numbers. The Sprint price comes from the live offer.

# Forward Deployed Engineer vs Solutions Engineer: Key Differences

URL: https://ghanemzadeh.com/forward-deployed-ai-engineer-vs-solutions-engineer/

[Forward Deployed AI Engineer](https://ghanemzadeh.com/forward-deployed-ai-engineer/)

## Forward Deployed AI Engineer vs solutions engineer

A Forward Deployed AI Engineer and a solutions engineer share the same technical, customer-facing instinct, but they work for different sides and ship different things. The Forward Deployed AI Engineer builds an AI workflow into the customer's own product and owns the result. The solutions engineer sells, demos, and integrates a vendor's product on the vendor's behalf.

By [Nasser Ghanemzadeh](https://ghanemzadeh.com/). Last updated October 2026.

### The short answer

If the code you ship lives in the customer's repository and the win is the customer's outcome, that is forward deployed work. If the code you ship is a demo or integration that helps close and onboard a customer onto your employer's platform, that is solutions engineering.

The two roles look similar from the outside because both put a technical person in front of a customer. The forward deployed engineer vs solutions engineer question comes down to whose product gets built and who you answer to.

### Side by side

| Dimension | Forward Deployed AI Engineer | Solutions engineer | Applied AI engineer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Works for | The customer's outcome, via a deployment company or a direct engagement | The software vendor selling the product | Their own company |
| Primary deliverable | A production AI workflow in the customer's codebase | Demos, proofs of concept, and integrations | AI features inside their own company's product |
| Where the code lives | The customer's product and repository | The vendor's platform and demo environments | Their employer's codebase |
| Measured on | A shipped workflow the customer's team can run and maintain | Pipeline, deals closed, and successful onboarding | Shipping AI capabilities in-house |
| AI focus | Prompt and context design, data integration, evaluation rubrics | Showing how the vendor's AI features fit the customer's stack | Building and evaluating AI features for their own product's users |
| Compensation | Base typically $160,000 to $220,000, median near $190,000; median US total compensation about $206,000; well above that at frontier labs, mostly in equity (sources below the table) | Varies by vendor; typically base plus commission (OTE), tied to sales and onboarding outcomes. | Varies by company and level |

Job postings in 2026 put a forward deployed engineer's base salary typically between $160,000 and $220,000, with a median near $190,000 ([Recruiting from Scratch](https://www.recruitingfromscratch.com/blog/forward-deployed-engineer-salary-in-2026-real-data-from-200k-job-postings)). Median US total compensation is about $206,000 ([Levels.fyi](https://www.levels.fyi/t/software-engineer/title/forward-deployed-engineer)). Pay at frontier labs such as Anthropic and OpenAI runs well above that, mostly in equity. Hiring for a small team? See [what a forward deployed engineer costs a startup](https://ghanemzadeh.com/forward-deployed-engineer-for-startups/).

### Where they overlap

Both roles need to read a customer's real environment quickly, translate a business problem into a technical plan, and stay credible in a room with engineers and executives at the same time. Both live with ambiguity and incomplete data. The instincts transfer cleanly, which is why solutions engineers are one of the most common backgrounds for people moving into forward deployed AI work.

### How to choose between them

Choose by what you want to own. If you want to close deals and help many customers adopt one product, solutions engineering fits. If you want to build the actual feature and own whether it works in production, the Forward Deployed AI Engineer role fits.

One more practical signal: seen as solutions engineer vs forward deployed engineer, the trade is breadth against depth. Solutions engineering rewards breadth across a pipeline; forward deployed work rewards depth on one customer at a time. Neither is more senior than the other. They optimize for different outcomes.

### Applied AI engineer vs solutions engineer vs forward deployed engineer

An applied AI engineer usually builds AI features into their own company's product, a solutions engineer sells and integrates a vendor's product, and a forward deployed engineer ships AI into a customer's product. The difference is whose codebase the work lives in: the employer's, the vendor's demo environment, or the customer's. One exception: at Anthropic, Applied AI is the customer-facing team, so an applied AI engineer there does forward deployed work. When a posting says applied AI, check whose product you would be building.

Running a B2B SaaS company? The FDE Sprint puts a forward deployed AI engineer on one workflow in your product and ships it in ten business days.

[Score your workflow (2 min)](https://ghanemzadeh.com/scorecard/)
[Book a 15-minute Scoping Call](https://ghanemzadeh.com/call/)

### Related

- [What is a Forward Deployed AI Engineer?](https://ghanemzadeh.com/forward-deployed-ai-engineer/)

- [How to become a Forward Deployed AI Engineer](https://ghanemzadeh.com/how-to-become-a-forward-deployed-ai-engineer/)

- [The book: Forward Deployed AI Engineering](https://ghanemzadeh.com/books/forward-deployed-ai-engineering/)

### Frequently asked questions

#### Can a solutions engineer become a Forward Deployed AI Engineer?

Often, yes. Solutions engineers already have the customer-facing instinct and the integration skills. The shift is from selling and configuring a vendor's product to building and owning a production AI workflow inside the customer's codebase, plus the evaluation discipline to prove it works.

#### Who does each role work for?

A solutions engineer almost always works for the software vendor and is measured on sales and onboarding. A Forward Deployed AI Engineer works on the customer's outcome, whether employed by a deployment company or engaged directly, and is measured on shipping a workflow the customer's team can run.

#### Does a solutions engineer write production code?

Sometimes, but usually demos, proofs of concept, and integrations rather than features that live permanently in the customer's product. A Forward Deployed AI Engineer's main deliverable is production code in the customer's repository, with edge cases, logging, and a handoff.

#### What is the difference between an applied AI engineer and a solutions engineer?

An applied AI engineer usually builds AI features inside their own company's product and is measured on shipping them; a solutions engineer sells, demos, and integrates a vendor's product for customers and is measured on the deal. At Anthropic the Applied AI title names the customer-facing team, which is closer to forward deployed work.

# What Is a Forward Deployed Engineer? The AI Role, Explained

URL: https://ghanemzadeh.com/forward-deployed-ai-engineer/

The role

## What Is a Forward Deployed Engineer?

**A Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) is a software engineer who sits at the customer's site and fills the gap between what the product does and what the customer needs, shipping working software, today usually an AI workflow, directly into the customer's systems.**

That definition comes from Bob McGrew, who spent 11 years at Palantir, where the role was invented, and later led research at OpenAI. This page covers what the work looks like, what it pays, who hires for it under which titles, and how to get in.

[Read the book →](https://ghanemzadeh.com/books/forward-deployed-ai-engineering/)
[See it as a service](https://ghanemzadeh.com/ai-feature-sprint/)

By [Nasser Ghanemzadeh](https://ghanemzadeh.com/). Last updated October 2026.

### What does a Forward Deployed Engineer do?

An FDE takes one narrow use case from a vague idea to a working AI feature inside the customer's product, end to end, and owns every step in between. The deliverable is code in the customer's repository.

A typical engagement runs through:

- **Scoping.** Turn "we should add AI" into one workflow with a named user, a clear input, and a clear output.

- **Architecture and UX.** Decide where the workflow lives in the product and how a person actually triggers and reviews it.

- **Prompt and context design.** Build the model interaction, including the system prompt, the retrieved context, and the guardrails.

- **Data integration.** Connect the workflow to the customer's real data and systems, often through the Model Context Protocol.

- **Implementation.** Write production code in the customer's repository, with edge cases, fallbacks, error states, and logging.

- **Evaluation.** Ship a written rubric that defines what good output looks like and how the team scores it over time.

- **Handoff.** Hand the team code they can maintain, plus the rubric and a short playbook, so the workflow survives without the engineer.

The output is code in the customer's repo. Not a dashboard. Not a report. Not a Loom.

### Why is it called "forward deployed"?

The phrase is military language. Forward deployed units are stationed at the edge, close to the situation, with the autonomy to act without calling headquarters first. Applied to engineers, it means the same thing: you work inside the customer's organization, and you decide on the spot.

Palantir made the term a job. It built its business on engineers who deploy into a customer's organization and deliver outcomes inside that customer's systems. The model spread because it solved a specific failure: software that works in a demo and dies in the customer's real environment.

In May 2026 the term went mainstream. Within a week, Anthropic and OpenAI each launched a new company to put engineers inside their customers: Anthropic's with Blackstone, Hellman & Friedman, and Goldman Sachs for mid-sized companies, and the OpenAI Deployment Company, built around Forward Deployed Engineers. Both aim to get frontier models working inside customers' products and operations rather than selling API access and hoping. The AI in some job titles marks the shift: the capability being deployed is no longer just software, it is an AI workflow.

### What does a Forward Deployed Engineer earn?

Job postings in 2026 put a forward deployed engineer's base salary typically between $160,000 and $220,000, with a median near $190,000 ([Recruiting from Scratch](https://www.recruitingfromscratch.com/blog/forward-deployed-engineer-salary-in-2026-real-data-from-200k-job-postings)). Median US total compensation is about $206,000 ([Levels.fyi](https://www.levels.fyi/t/software-engineer/title/forward-deployed-engineer)). Pay at frontier labs such as Anthropic and OpenAI runs well above that, mostly in equity.

| Compensation measure | Figure (2026) |
| --- | --- |
| Base salary, typical range (2026 job postings) | $160,000 to $220,000 |
| Median base salary (2026 job postings) | About $190,000 |
| Median US total compensation | About $206,000 |
| Median posted base range, US engineering roles (my count of 260 live roles, October 2026) | $180,000 to $250,208 |
| Frontier labs such as Anthropic and OpenAI | Well above that, mostly in equity |

Posted ranges run higher than surveys of what people are paid, because a range runs to the top of the band. My [October 2026 count of 260 live forward deployed roles at 44 companies](https://ghanemzadeh.com/forward-deployed-engineer-job-market/) has the full pay, travel, location, and skills data, with the dataset to download.

Base salary figures are from Recruiting from Scratch's analysis of 2026 job postings; total compensation is from Levels.fyi's US data. Individual offers vary with seniority, location, and equity. For how that lands on a small team's budget, see [what a forward deployed engineer costs a startup](https://ghanemzadeh.com/forward-deployed-engineer-for-startups/). To buy FDE time instead of hiring, the [FDE-as-a-service market map](https://ghanemzadeh.com/fde-as-a-service/) lists 33 providers and every price they publish.

### FDE titles by company

Almost nobody posts this job under one name. The same customer-embedded, ship-into-production role is hired under different titles at different companies, so searching for one string misses most of the market.

| Company | What they call the role |
| --- | --- |
| Palantir | Echo and Delta, the two halves of its forward deployed practice |
| OpenAI | Forward Deployed Engineer |
| Anthropic | Applied AI |
| Sierra | Agent Engineer |
| Harvey | Implementation Engineer |
| Decagon | Agent builder / agent SWE |

Echo and Delta are defined in the [glossary](https://ghanemzadeh.com/glossary/), and the split between them is a core chapter of [the book](https://ghanemzadeh.com/books/forward-deployed-ai-engineering/).

### How is an FDE different from a solutions engineer?

A solutions engineer works for the vendor and is measured on the sale; an FDE works on the customer's outcome and is measured on what ships. Both are technical and customer-facing, which is why the two roles are so often confused.

| Role | What they ship | Where the work lives | Optimizes for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Forward Deployed AI Engineer | A working AI workflow built into the customer's product | The customer's codebase and product | A shipped outcome the customer's team can run and maintain |
| Solutions engineer | Integrations, demos, and configuration of a vendor's product | The boundary between vendor and customer | Closing and onboarding the customer onto the vendor's platform |
| ML engineer | Models, training pipelines, and inference infrastructure | The model and data platform | Model performance, scale, and reliability |
| AI consultant | Strategy, roadmaps, and recommendations | Documents and meetings | Advice and direction, with execution left to others |

For a side-by-side that goes deeper on the closest comparison, see [Forward Deployed AI Engineer vs solutions engineer](https://ghanemzadeh.com/forward-deployed-ai-engineer-vs-solutions-engineer/).

### Why did the FDE role explode in 2026?

Because enterprises learned that buying AI is not the same as deploying it. An MIT study cited in the book found that 95% of enterprise AI pilots produce no measurable return. The FDE is the industry's answer to that gap, and in 2026 the money followed.

- **May 2026.** On May 4, Anthropic announced a new AI services company with Blackstone, Hellman & Friedman, and Goldman Sachs. Days later, OpenAI launched the OpenAI Deployment Company, with more than $4 billion of investment at a $10 billion valuation, built around Forward Deployed Engineers.

- **May 16, 2026.** Business Insider reported that Indeed postings for the role grew from 643 in April 2025 to 5,330 in April 2026, more than 700% in a year. The same month, the title returned 55,000+ LinkedIn results in the US and over 100 postings on the YC job board.

- **June 30, 2026.** AWS announced a $1 billion FDE program.

- **July 2, 2026.** Microsoft launched Frontier: $2.5 billion and 6,000 embedded experts.

- **July 30, 2026.** [TechCrunch reported](https://techcrunch.com/2026/07/30/forward-deployed-engineers-are-the-ai-industrys-latest-talent-obsession/) a C&T study projecting demand for FDEs to surge 2,100% by the end of 2026, against an estimated 2,000 qualified FDEs in total.

### What skills does the role require?

Less model research, more product engineering and judgment. The hard part is usually deciding what to build and proving it works, not calling the API.

- **Product engineering.** Shipping real features into a real codebase, with the discipline that production demands.

- **Prompt and context design.** Getting reliable output from frontier models, including retrieval and structured context.

- **Data integration.** Connecting models to messy customer systems and APIs, often via [MCP](https://ghanemzadeh.com/glossary/#mcp).

- **Evaluation.** Defining what good output is and scoring it, so quality is measured rather than asserted.

- **Customer-facing judgment.** Scoping under pressure, saying no to the wrong workflow, and protecting a fixed timeline.

### How do you become a Forward Deployed Engineer?

Most people who do this well arrive from product engineering, solutions or consulting, or a founder background, then prove they can ship one narrow AI workflow end to end.

The fastest credible path is to build and ship a real workflow, write the evaluation rubric for it, and be able to walk someone through the code. For a step-by-step version, see [how to become a Forward Deployed AI Engineer](https://ghanemzadeh.com/how-to-become-a-forward-deployed-ai-engineer/).

### Forward Deployed AI Engineering for founder-led B2B SaaS

The enterprise version of this role is built for Fortune 500 procurement. The same work, sized for a 5-to-50-person founder-led SaaS team, is the FDE Sprint: one narrow AI workflow shipped into the product in 10 business days, fixed scope and fixed price.

That's the work I do. Most patterns I ship into a customer's codebase have already run in [Vectig](https://vectig.com), my own AI-native product and live R&D lab. If you want to see the engagement, start with the [FDE Sprint](https://ghanemzadeh.com/ai-feature-sprint/) or a [Discovery Day](https://ghanemzadeh.com/discovery-day/).

Weighing a full-time hire against a contractor or a Sprint? Start with [Does a startup need a forward deployed engineer?](https://ghanemzadeh.com/forward-deployed-engineer-for-startups/)

Running a B2B SaaS company? The FDE Sprint puts a forward deployed AI engineer on one workflow in your product and ships it in ten business days.

### Frequently asked questions

#### Do Forward Deployed Engineers write production code?

Yes. The defining deliverable is working code in the customer's repository, with edge cases, fallbacks, error states, logging, and a handoff the customer's team can maintain. Demos and decks are what the role exists to replace.

#### Is Forward Deployed Engineer a good career in 2026?

The demand data is unusually one-sided. Indeed postings grew more than 700% in a year per Business Insider, TechCrunch reports projected demand growth of 2,100% by the end of 2026 against an estimated 2,000 qualified FDEs, and median US total compensation is about $206,000. The constraint is proving you can do the work, not finding openings.

#### Do you need a machine learning background to become an FDE?

No. The role applies existing models rather than training them. The core skills are product engineering, prompt and context design, data integration, evaluation, and customer-facing judgment. A research or MLOps background helps in some engagements but is not the entry requirement.

#### How much travel does the role involve?

More than most software roles. Anthropic's listing puts travel at 25 percent. OpenAI expects its FDEs on customer sites a few days a week during an engagement. At Palantir, Nabeel Qureshi describes four to five days a week at the customer's office as the high end; two to three is more typical.

#### Is a Forward Deployed Engineer the same as an applied AI engineer?

Functionally, yes. Applied AI is Anthropic's title for the FDE-shaped role, the same way Sierra says Agent Engineer and Harvey says Implementation Engineer. The employer's label changes; the work of shipping AI into a customer's production systems does not.

# Forward Deployed Engineers for Startups: 3 Ways to Get One

URL: https://ghanemzadeh.com/forward-deployed-engineer-for-startups/

[Forward Deployed Engineer](https://ghanemzadeh.com/forward-deployed-ai-engineer/)

## Does a startup need a forward deployed engineer?

Usually not a full-time one. A startup under 50 people rarely needs a full-time forward deployed engineer. It needs one AI workflow shipped into its product and a team that can maintain it afterward. There are three ways to get there: hire one, contract one, or run a fixed-scope Sprint.

By [Nasser Ghanemzadeh](https://ghanemzadeh.com/). Last updated October 2026.

### Option 1: hire one full-time

A full-time forward deployed engineer ships AI features inside your codebase and stays to maintain them. That is the right call when AI work is continuous: several workflows a quarter, each with its own data, users, and evaluation.

Job postings in 2026 put a forward deployed engineer's base salary typically between $160,000 and $220,000, with a median near $190,000 ([Recruiting from Scratch](https://www.recruitingfromscratch.com/blog/forward-deployed-engineer-salary-in-2026-real-data-from-200k-job-postings)). Median US total compensation is about $206,000 ([Levels.fyi](https://www.levels.fyi/t/software-engineer/title/forward-deployed-engineer)). That's roughly $16,000 a month in base salary alone, before equity, benefits, and the months it takes to hire.

Hiring usually takes months. The pool of engineers who have taken AI to production is small, and the strong ones are interviewing everywhere. Onboarding comes on top of that before the first workflow ships.

Hire when you have a year of AI work to give one engineer, and a technical leader who can manage and judge their output.

### Option 2: contract a freelancer or agency

A freelancer or agency gives you engineering capacity without a hire. You can usually start sooner than a full-time search allows, pay only while the work runs, and stop when it's done.

Where it usually breaks:

- **Scope.** Hourly and open-ended engagements drift. Without a one-sentence scope agreed on the first day, "add AI to the product" turns into three half-built features.

- **Handoff.** When the contractor leaves, the knowledge leaves with them. If nobody on your team can run, debug, or change the workflow, you own code you can't maintain.

- **Evaluation.** Few contracts define what good output looks like. Without a rubric and test cases, nobody can tell whether a prompt change made the workflow better or worse.

Contract when the scope is already tight, someone on your team will own the result, and the contract names acceptance criteria and a handoff. Weighing an agency specifically? See [AI agency vs forward deployed engineer](https://ghanemzadeh.com/ai-agency-vs-forward-deployed-engineer/). To compare the firms and platforms that rent out FDEs specifically, see the [FDE-as-a-service market map](https://ghanemzadeh.com/fde-as-a-service/).

### Option 3: a fixed-scope FDE Sprint

The FDE Sprint is the fixed-scope version: one AI workflow, scoped on Day 1, running on your data by Day 5, and in your repo by Day 10. A forward deployed AI engineer does the build inside your codebase, then hands over a recorded walkthrough, an output rubric, and a playbook your team uses to maintain it. The price is fixed, with a full refund if there's no working prototype by Day 5 or the workflow isn't running to its acceptance criteria by Day 10. [See how the Sprint works](https://ghanemzadeh.com/ai-feature-sprint/).

### How to choose

The deciding question is how much AI work you have, and who will own it once it ships. A team with one workflow in mind and no AI engineer on staff is usually best served by a Sprint first, then a hire once the second and third workflows are queued. To run your own numbers, use the [FDE cost calculator](https://ghanemzadeh.com/fde-cost-calculator/).

| Option | Cost | Time to first shipped workflow | Who owns it after | Best when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hire full-time | Highest: a senior engineering salary plus equity, every month | Months: the search, then onboarding | Your team, through the new hire | AI is a year-round roadmap, not one feature |
| Contract a freelancer or agency | Variable: hourly or monthly, open-ended unless scoped | Weeks to months, depending on scope | Often the contractor, unless the contract includes a handoff | The scope is tight and someone in-house will own the result |
| Fixed-scope Sprint | Fixed: $5,000, half on signing | Ten business days | Your team, with a rubric, playbook, and walkthrough | You want one workflow live fast and your team to run it |

### What to have ready before any of them

Whichever route you pick, four things decide whether the first workflow ships on time. The [Workflow Scorecard](https://ghanemzadeh.com/scorecard/) checks all four in two minutes, along with eight dimensions of the idea itself.

- Read-only codebase access that can be granted within a week.

- Sample data that exists and can be shared.

- One decision-maker who answers within a business day.

- A data processing agreement with your model provider, such as Anthropic or OpenAI.

### Frequently asked questions

#### Can a startup afford a forward deployed engineer?

Rarely as a full-time hire before it has a year of AI work to give one. Forward deployed engineers are paid at rates set by frontier labs and enterprise deployment companies, so most startups get the same work through a contract or a fixed-scope Sprint first, and hire once AI is a standing part of the roadmap.

#### What's the difference between an FDE and an AI consultant?

An FDE ships working code into your product; an AI consultant usually delivers advice, a strategy, or a roadmap. The FDE's work lives in your repository and is judged by whether it runs on your data. The consultant's work is a document your team still has to build.

#### How long does it take to ship a first AI feature?

Ten business days for one narrow workflow, if codebase access and sample data are ready on Day 1. Broader features take longer, and most of the delay before that point is scoping and data access, not engineering.

#### What should the first AI workflow be?

One narrow, internal workflow that drafts something a person reviews, runs at least weekly, and uses data you already have in one place. Investor updates, support ticket summaries, and customer account summaries are typical first choices: one user, one input, one output, and a human check before anything leaves.

Weighing a Sprint for your first workflow? Pick a candidate from the [AI workflow library for B2B SaaS](https://ghanemzadeh.com/ai-workflows-for-saas/), [score it](https://ghanemzadeh.com/scorecard/) in two minutes, then [book a 15-minute Scoping Call](https://ghanemzadeh.com/call/).

# Forward Deployed Engineer Jobs: 260 Roles Analyzed (2026)

URL: https://ghanemzadeh.com/forward-deployed-engineer-job-market/

[Forward Deployed Engineer](https://ghanemzadeh.com/forward-deployed-ai-engineer/)

## Forward deployed engineer jobs in October 2026: 260 roles at 44 companies, analyzed

On October 12, 2026, I pulled every live forward deployed role from the public job boards of 144 AI and software companies. 44 were hiring: 382 postings, 260 distinct roles. In the US, the median posted base range for a forward deployed engineer is $180,000 to $250,000. More than half of the roles that state a travel figure allow for 50% or more. And the title is spreading well beyond engineering.

By [Nasser Ghanemzadeh](https://ghanemzadeh.com/). Data collected October 12, 2026. [Download the data (CSV)](https://ghanemzadeh.com/assets/data/fde-job-postings-2026-10-12.csv).

### The numbers

- **44 companies, 260 distinct roles, 382 postings.** Databricks, Palantir, and OpenAI alone account for half of the roles.

- **Median US posted base range: $180,000 to $250,208.** Median midpoint $216,104 across 74 engineering roles; $220,552 if each company counts once.

- **88% of US engineering roles post a salary range,** so the pay figures cover nearly the whole US market in this sample.

- **56% mention travel; 42% put a number on it.** The most common figure is up to 50% of the time.

- **58% of roles are in the US, 40% outside it.** London has more than any other city outside the US, with 36.

- **Python (67%), agents (55%), TypeScript or JavaScript (54%), and evals (48%)** are what engineering postings ask for most.

- **A quarter of engineering roles mention a security clearance.** Government and defense are a large share of the work.

- **42% of roles are not engineering roles.** Companies now hire forward deployed bankers, lawyers, strategists, architects, and product managers.

### Who is hiring

The sixteen companies with the most forward deployed roles. A distinct role is one title at one company, counted once however many cities it is posted in; Databricks, for example, posts most of its roles once per city.

Pay figures cover the 74 distinct engineering roles in the US that post a salary range in US dollars, which is 88% of them. They are base salary ranges as posted, not offers or total compensation; equity and bonus come on top at most of these companies. Where a posting gives one range per location, the first range is used.

- **Median range:** $180,000 to $250,208.

- **Median midpoint:** $216,104, and the middle half of roles fall between $170,000 and $242,500.

- **Company-weighted median midpoint:** $220,552 across 26 companies, so the three biggest hirers don't set the number on their own.

- **By level:** staff and principal roles have a median midpoint of $250,000 (5 roles), senior roles $216,104 (15), and roles with no level in the title $215,000 (53). Level barely moves the midpoint below staff.

- **Lowest and highest:** $90,000 at the bottom of a Palantir US Government security role, $445,000 at the top of OpenAI's Forward Deployed Security Engineer range.

### How much travel

The forward deployed engineer is embedded with the customer, and the postings say so. 56% of roles mention travel and 42% state a percentage. Where a posting gives a range, such as Palantir's "25 to 75% within country," the table counts the upper bound.

| Stated travel | Roles |

| Up to 50% | 54 |
| Up to 75% | 7 |
| Up to 80% | 1 |
| Up to 90% | 1 |

57% of the roles that state a figure allow for 50% or more. The figure tracks the company more than the role: OpenAI's postings mostly say up to 50%, Databricks' mostly 20%, Cohere's 20 to 40%, and Shield AI's about 30%.

### Where the jobs are

152 roles (58%) are in the US and 103 (40%) are outside it; 5 are remote with no country given. Outside the US, London leads with 36 roles, then Tokyo (9), Singapore (8), Paris (7), and Munich (6). 32% of roles allow remote work in at least one location, which is low for software jobs in 2026 and fits a role defined by being on site.

The job is building with models, not training them. Agents and evals each appear in about half of the postings; fine-tuning or post-training in 13%. Palantir accounts for half of the roles that mention a clearance, followed by the government and public-sector teams at Databricks, Cohere, OpenAI, and Vannevar Labs.

### The title is spreading

Forward deployed started as an engineering title. In October 2026 it is a way of working that companies attach to other jobs.

| Role family | Distinct roles | Share |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Engineer | 151 | 58% |
| Strategist, architect, or domain specialist | 45 | 17% |
| Manager or leader | 39 | 15% |
| Intern or new grad | 19 | 7% |
| Product manager | 6 | 2% |

Rogo hires forward deployed bankers and investors. Eudia hires forward deployed lawyers. Harvey hires forward deployed finance engineers for private credit, buyouts, and real estate. Cursor hires forward deployed strategists, Notion forward deployed architects, and Scale AI and Cresta forward deployed product managers. The common thread is the one in the original Palantir model: a specialist who sits with the customer and makes the product work inside their business.

Most engineering titles carry no level at all (113 of 151). Of those that do, senior (25) and staff or principal (11) far outnumber junior (2). The entry points are internships and new-grad programs, 19 roles, nearly all at Palantir.

### What it means

**For founders.** A forward deployed engineer is priced by OpenAI, Databricks, and Palantir. A median posted midpoint above $216,000, before equity, is hard to justify for a startup with one or two AI workflows to ship; [the three ways to get one](https://ghanemzadeh.com/forward-deployed-engineer-for-startups/) compares hiring with contracting and a fixed-scope Sprint.

**For engineers.** The postings describe the job plainly: Python and TypeScript, agents and evals, a customer you sit with, and a suitcase. [How to become a forward deployed engineer](https://ghanemzadeh.com/how-to-become-a-forward-deployed-ai-engineer/) turns that list into a path.
